feature.label: General SEM PLS Multiple-Mediation Full-Model Percentile Bootstrap

claim.supported_scope: Opt-in Experimental Labs execution for parallel, serial, and mixed multiple-mediation effects in a supported single-group recursive General SEM PLS composite model, using deterministic full-model case resampling, two-sided Type-7 percentile intervals, sample standard errors, plus-one probabilities, and an explicit 90% usable-replicate gate.
claim.estimand: Stable specific path products plus source-target total indirect and total effects, recomputed after a complete PLS model refit for each usable indexed case-resample.
assumptions: The schema-6 project is newly created with general_sem_v1 authority and the compiled structural graph is acyclic.
The model and raw continuous data satisfy the exact CompiledPlsPlanV2 scoring boundary and listwise-deletion policy.
Every effect and inference receipt remains bound to the same recipe, model, dataset, compiled plan, seed, and typed capability identity.
exclusions: Feedback, reciprocal, multigroup, interaction, higher-order, constrained, common-factor, covariance-input, weighted, clustered, and stratified models are excluded.
Conditional probes, lazy path materialization, BCa, studentized, and one-sided inference are excluded.
Causal mediation identification, counterfactual effects, and observed-variable PROCESS workflows are separate concerns.
warnings: Engine evidence includes a bounded independent unstandardized observed-score reference simulation for path products, bootstrap means, Type-7 percentile truth inclusion, and the usable-replicate gate only; it never calls production Rust and does not establish standardized PLS scoring, sample-SE or plus-one-probability behavior, null calibration, full PLS-PM refit simulation, archive, native qualification, export, packaged Windows, SmartPLS numerical parity, or release evidence.
A statistically nonzero indirect effect does not by itself establish a causal mechanism.

equations.expression: specific_p = product_{e in p} beta_e; total_indirect_ij = sum_{p in P_ij,length(p)>=2} specific_p

references.citation: SmartPLS public mediation documentation and its cited mediation literature
Validation-only independent path-product, Type-7, sample-SE, plus-one, and usable-gate micro-reference

simulations.design: Ninety-six deterministic unstandardized observed-score mixed-mediation trials with 240 rows each. Every trial independently refits the complete downstream OLS path system in 199 case bootstraps and evaluates three focal X-to-Y specific indirect effects plus the focal total indirect and total effect; production Rust is not called or compared.
simulations.seed_policy: Frozen scenario-indexed data and bootstrap seeds with an exact replay check; singular fits count as failed refits and the 90 percent publication boundary is tested on and below its threshold.
simulations.acceptance_rule: All deterministic checks pass; absolute bias <= 0.025, absolute relative bias <= 0.10, RMSE <= 0.15, absolute mean bootstrap bias <= 0.02, and at least 82 of 96 Type-7 percentile intervals include the truth for every frozen focal effect. Hit counts and descriptive Wilson intervals are reported. This is a bounded engine smoke reference, not nominal-coverage qualification or a full PLS-PM simulation oracle.

boundaries.case: A bootstrap sample is constant, singular, nonconvergent, or cannot estimate a requested path.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Record the indexed typed failure; publish no result if usable replicates fall below max(2, ceil(0.9B)).

boundaries.case: The graph contains feedback, an interaction, a higher-order construct, a conditional probe, lazy materialization, or another unsupported scoring semantic.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Preserve the model and return a corrective blocked capability decision without silently dropping semantics.

boundaries.case: Rows, declarations, constructs, indicators, or eligible labels are consistently permuted, or permitted scale/location transformations are applied.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Mapped effect identities and scientific summaries remain equivalent under the frozen preprocessing and orientation contract.

boundaries.case: The same valid recipe is replayed with one and four supported workers.
boundaries.expected_behavior: The scientific result, replicate ledger, and usable-index digest are identical after normalizing worker metadata.

boundaries.case: A recipe, model, dataset, plan, effect identity, interval, p-value ledger, method version, or receipt digest is altered.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Strict schema-6 authority validation rejects the attachment and no partial result is shown.

tamper_tests.expected_behavior: Reject a result whose exact General SEM mediation-bootstrap capability differs from its recipe and receipt.
Reject a result relabeled with another bootstrap or mediation version.
Reject a result whose resident dataset fingerprint differs.
Reject a changed project member or canonical attachment digest.
Reject duplicate keys, unknown fields, invalid counts, non-finite values, unordered identities, or inconsistent effect ledgers.
Never attach this identity to historical projects or results without general_sem_v1 authority.

persistence.legacy_policy: This capability applies only to newly created schema-6 general_sem_v1 projects; no legacy migration or upgrade-copy route is provided.

applicability_blockers: Failed point fit or insufficient usable bootstrap replicates
result_surfaces: Bootstrap standard errors, intervals, and probabilities
native.gui_cli_parity_rule: For identical recipe, model, data, seed, compiler plan, and workers, all product surfaces must read the same canonical result. The same-app native schema-6 General SEM project-mode workflow is connected from dataset/model activation through execution, canonical result persistence, close, and reopen, but independent cross-surface, packaged, and release qualification remain pending.
accessibility_rules: Every effect, interval, probability, failure, and unavailable reason is available in an accessible table.
Support and error states remain understandable without color, diagram position, or pointer-only interaction.
